member.name: M:KeshavSingh.Auth.AuthEngine.AuthenticateSocialAsync(System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Social sign-in (e.g. GitHub), verified-identity-first: the caller has ALREADY confirmed with the provider (OAuth + that provider's own verified-email API) before calling this — this method itself does no provider talk, just policy: - Link-only, never creates an account: an unmatched email is a hard failure, not a signup. - Two-factor is MANDATORY here regardless of toggles (those govern the email/SMS/WhatsApp FALLBACK channels for password login, not whether 2FA applies at all). An account with no TOTP enrolled is refused outright — enroll it via password login first. - Every accepted sign-in still goes through the SAME 2FA step-token challenge password login uses, so VerifyTwoFactorAsync (and every existing 2FA UI/endpoint) needs no changes.

member.name: T:KeshavSingh.Auth.RequirePagePermissionAttribute
member.summary:
Real API-level enforcement of an app's own fine-grained page/permission model — e.g. an admin console's page.* keys, driven by which custom role/group grants a user holds. A bare [Authorize] endpoint is reachable by any signed-in user regardless of that app's own permission model; this closes that gap without hard-coding any single app's role/permission shape.
The actual decision is delegated to an app-registered (DI), so this attribute has no idea what a "page" or a "grant" means for any particular app — including whether some role bypasses the check entirely, which is the evaluator's call to make. No evaluator registered means fail CLOSED (403), not open. Denials return 403 with a plain-language reason rather than a bare status code, and never a stack trace.

member.name: T:KeshavSingh.Auth.SsoCookieOptions
member.summary:
Bindable options (config section "Sso") for the cross-subdomain single-sign-on cookie that carries the rotating refresh token. The cookie is the ONLY place the refresh token lives on the client — it is never returned in a response body and is HttpOnly so no script (on any origin) can read it.
Shared by every app in the *.keshavsingh.in family so they all issue/read an identical cookie shape; keeping this in one package (instead of copy-pasted per app) is what makes the SSO contract safe to reason about.
In production the cookie is scoped to the parent domain (e.g. ".keshavsingh.in") so every sibling site (admin.keshavsingh.in, git.keshavsingh.in, …) sends it and can silently obtain an access token from this identity provider. In development leave empty and false so it works over http://localhost.

member.name: P:KeshavSingh.Auth.SsoCookieOptions.CookieName
member.summary: Cookie name. Kept opaque; not security-sensitive.

member.name: P:KeshavSingh.Auth.SsoCookieOptions.Domain
member.summary: Cookie Domain. Set to the leading-dot parent domain in production (".keshavsingh.in"). Empty/null pins the cookie to the current host — the correct behaviour for localhost.

member.name: P:KeshavSingh.Auth.SsoCookieOptions.Secure

member.summary: SameSite mode. "Lax" is correct here: all apps share the registrable domain, so cross-subdomain requests are same-site and the cookie is sent (with CORS credentials).

member.summary:
Bindable options (config section "WebAuthn") for FIDO2 passkeys. Shared across every app in the *.keshavsingh.in family that offers passkey login, so the relying-party contract can't drift between them.
must be a registrable-domain suffix of every origin that runs the passkey ceremonies. Using the parent domain ("keshavsingh.in") means a passkey works across every sibling app (admin., id., …) — the same reason the SSO cookie is scoped to the parent.
is the exact allowlist of browser origins the WebAuthn library will accept in clientDataJSON. Only origins that actually run navigator.credentials (the login and security pages) belong here — never a wildcard.
